# browser-mcp

A Playwright-backed Model Context Protocol server providing browser primitives plus domain plugins for design audits, WordPress block development, and Gutenberg authoring.

This file is the consumer-facing manual for agents that *invoke* browser-mcp tools. If you're building or extending the server itself, read the source — this file omits per-line code detail and stays at the contract surface, with source-tree pointers (§ Plugins and modes) for finding the implementation behind a behavior.

## TL;DR {#tldr}

- Browser primitives (navigate, click, screenshot, evaluate, ...) plus four pluggable domains: `dev`, `design-compare`, `wp`, `wp-gutenberg`. Each plugin registers tools.
- A **mode** is a session-level auth/setup bundle that a plugin can also register (e.g. `wp` registers the `wordpress` mode that injects WordPress admin auth into the BrowserContext). Modes are NOT a gate on which tools are available — they layer hooks onto sessions. `mcp__browser__list_modes` enumerates registered modes.
- Tools accept an optional `session_id` to attach to a persistent context (from `open_session`); without it each call spins an ephemeral session and discards it on return.
- Comparison tools (`compare_element`, `compare_screenshot`, `visual_diff`, `design_audit`) report different score conventions and accept different mask APIs — see § Cross-cutting concepts before mixing them.
- `align_elements` is a measurement tool, not a comparison tool: it returns the per-element (dx, dy) translation that best matches the reference, grounded in pixel SAD over the live screenshot. Use it when DOM-reported coordinates are suspect — see § Surfaces › `align_elements`.
- All coordinates the tool produces or consumes are **HTML viewport pixels**. Values from non-viewport sources (Figma canvas, Figma node-relative) carry their own coordinate frame and must be converted before they cross the API boundary — see § Coordinate spaces.

## Plugins and modes {#modes-and-plugins}

The server boots with a plugin set defined by the `BROWSER_MCP_PLUGINS` env var (comma-separated, e.g. `dev,wp,wp-gutenberg,design-compare`). Each plugin can:

- **Register tools** (the `mcp__browser__*` surface). A tool is available whenever its registering plugin is loaded — there's no per-tool mode gate.
- **Register modes** as session-level auth/setup bundles. A mode is a set of hooks (e.g. inject auth cookies before any tool runs in this session) that consumers opt into per session. Currently the `wp` plugin registers the `wordpress` mode (WordPress admin auth injection); no other plugin registers a mode.
- **Declare required env vars and dependencies** on other plugins.

**Tolerant loader.** A plugin with a missing required env var is silently skipped, and its dependents cascade-skip (e.g. `wp-gutenberg` skips when `wp` skips for a missing `WP_URL`). Stderr carries the warning; the server still boots and unaffected plugins still work. Hard errors only fire on real config bugs (sealed registry, name collision, undeclared dependency, tool/action/mode collision).

> **Hazard:** if `mcp__browser__list_modes` returns "No modes registered" or an expected mode is missing, the cause is almost always a silently-skipped plugin from missing env. See § Diagnosis › Mode not registered for the fix recipe.

**MCP scopes replace, do not merge.** When the same server name (`browser`) appears in both `~/.claude.json` (user scope) and a project-local `.mcp.json`, the project entry **fully replaces** the user entry. There is no env-block merge. If a project needs a different `WP_URL`, the project entry must duplicate the full env block, not just the override.

**Where plugins live in source.** `src/plugins/dev`, `src/plugins/design-compare`, `src/plugins/wp`, `src/plugins/wp-gutenberg`. Plugin manifests at `src/plugins/<name>/index.ts`. Tool implementations under `src/plugins/<name>/tools/` (or `src/core/` for primitives). The plugin registry (`src/plugins/registry.ts`) enforces the dependency graph and the cascade-skip behavior.

## Command index {#command-index}

Exhaustive list of `mcp__browser__*` tools by plugin. Tools marked **(contract)** have a deep treatment in § Surfaces; the rest are routine and have a one-line entry only. Use this table to pick the right tool, then dive to the contract section if the tool is non-trivial.

### dev plugin

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `screenshot` | Full-page or clipped PNG screenshot | core primitive |
| `element_screenshot` | Element-bbox-cropped screenshot | core primitive |
| `visual_diff` | Pixelmatch two PNGs, optional crop | (contract) compare-tool selection |
| `compare_screenshot` | Live URL ↔ reference PNG, full-page | (contract) compare-tool selection, mask, coverage |
| `compare_element` | Live URL ↔ reference PNG, element-cropped | (contract) compare-tool selection, mask, alignment, coverage |
| `align_elements` | Per-element pixel-shift measurement vs reference PNG; applies CSS transforms to confirm | (contract) align-vs-compare selection |
| `console_capture` | Capture console messages over a script run | |
| `dom_snapshot` | Full DOM tree as JSON | |
| `dom_query` | Batched DOM read by selector with typed schema (text/rect/computed/attributes per query) | preferred over raw `evaluate_script` for element discovery |
| `accessibility_snapshot` | a11y tree + 6 hand-rolled rule asserts | (surface) accessibility_snapshot — NOT a full WCAG audit; also the cheapest discovery tool for clickables-by-role+name |
| `list_interactive_elements` | Every clickable / typable on the page with role + name + rect + click-ready `selector_hint` | preferred entry point for "what can I click here?" — bundled discovery, one call |
| `axe_audit` | Full axe-core WCAG audit (violations + passes + incomplete) | (surface) axe_audit; session-aware |
| `network_log` | HAR-style network requests over a script run | |
| `page_metadata` | Title, URL, meta tags | |
| `performance_metrics` | LCP, FCP, TTFB | |
| `computed_styles` | `getComputedStyle()` for selector | |
| `evaluate_script` | Run JS in page context, return result | **reach for last** — use dedicated tools for click / type / discovery / wait first |
| `trace_start` / `trace_stop` | Playwright trace zip | |
| `schema_extract` | JSON-LD / microdata / OG tags | |

### design-compare plugin

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `design_compare` | CSS-property comparison live ↔ design spec | (contract) compare-tool selection |
| `design_audit` | `design_compare` + visual diff + cross-reference | (contract) compare-tool selection, hide, coverage |

### wp plugin

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `wp` | WordPress admin login + REST helpers | requires `WP_URL`; optional `WP_USERNAME` / `WP_PASSWORD` |

### wp-gutenberg plugin

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `insert_block` | Add a block to current post | depends on `wp`; `inner_blocks` seeds nested children; `save: true` persists; auto-targets the editable post body on `template-locked` FSE posts (pass `root_client_id` to override) |
| `get_blocks` | Read current post's block tree | |
| `screenshot_block` | Crop screenshot to block bbox | |
| `inspect_toolbar` | Block toolbar state | |
| `compare_block` | `compare_element` scoped to a block | (contract) compare-tool selection |
| `evaluate` | JS in editor iframe context | |
| `check_block` | Validity / breakage check | inserts into the post body (not the locked canvas root) on `template-locked` FSE posts |
| `publish` | Save + publish current post | |
| `block_html` | Normalized editor + frontend HTML for structural diff | strips Gutenberg noise; `strip_attributes` / `strip_classes` / `strip_css_vars` / `strip_subtrees` for project-specific runtime artifacts; `source: "auto"\|"template"\|"post_content"` resolves the target in the canvas tree or in the parsed post body (auto-detected on block-theme posts) |
| `clear_blocks` | Empty the post | clears the post body and leaves the surrounding template intact on `template-locked` FSE posts; returns the number of body blocks removed |

> **Hazard (block-theme posts & `core/post-content` leaf).** In WP 6.5+ block themes, the post editor mounts a canvas template tree where `core/post-content` is a renderer leaf and the post body blocks live in a nested `useEntityBlockEditor("postType","post")` provider — invisible to `wp.data.select("core/block-editor").getBlocks()`. `block_html` defaults to `source: "auto"`: if the canvas tree contains a `core/post-content` leaf, it parses `wp.data.select("core/editor").getEditedPostContent()` instead and resolves the target there. On classic-theme posts auto is a no-op (no leaf → uses canvas tree). Pass `source: "template"` to force the canvas-tree path or `source: "post_content"` to force parsing. In `post_content` mode `client_id` is rejected (parsed blocks have synthetic clientIds); use `block_name`, `block_path`, or `block_index`. The `client_id` field in the response reports the inner-store clientId read off the located `[data-block]` element. This read-side `source` flag is only on `block_html` for now; `get_blocks`, `compare_block`, `screenshot_block`, `inspect_toolbar` haven't been extended pending a consumer ask. (The mutation tools `insert_block` / `check_block` / `clear_blocks` handle the same canvas-tree case automatically — see the next hazard.)

> **Hazard (block-theme posts & canvas-root insertion).** On `template-locked` FSE posts the OUTER `core/block-editor` store top level is the locked template canvas (`core/template-part → main → core/post-content → core/template-part`); dispatching `insertBlock` / `resetBlocks` there is **silently rejected** — the block lands nowhere and never reaches the saved post body, yielding false-negative `check_block` verdicts. The editable post body is the *controlled inner-block list* of the `core/post-content` block, reachable in the SAME store via that block's clientId — `getBlockOrder(pcId)` / `getBlocks(pcId)` / `getBlock(cid)` see it and `insertBlock(block, idx, pcId)` syncs into `getEditedPostContent()` (no nested entity-store dispatch needed; `getBlocks()` with no clientId only walks the serialized template tree, which is why the body looks empty from the top level). So `insert_block` and `check_block` resolve the `core/post-content` clientId and insert there (pass `insert_block`'s `root_client_id` to override); `clear_blocks` empties only that block's inner list, preserving the template. On classic-theme / `post-only` posts there is no `core/post-content` leaf, so all three fall back to top-level insert / `resetBlocks([])` — behaviorally unchanged.

> **Hazard (WP_URL host binding).** Every `wp-gutenberg` post-editing tool routes through `navigateToEditor`, which builds `${WP_URL}/wp-admin/post.php?post=${post_id}&action=edit` and navigates there. The env-var `WP_URL` is the host these tools drive — passing a `session_id` authed against a different host (e.g. staging) is not sufficient to retarget the tool; the call will yank the page to `WP_URL`'s host, where the post likely doesn't exist or the session has no cookies. **Detect-and-skip:** when the page is already on `/wp-admin/post.php?post=${post_id}&action=edit` (on any host), the tool skips the navigation — so the working pattern for a non-`WP_URL` host is to first navigate the session to that host's editor URL yourself (via `navigate({ session_id, url })`), then call the `wp-gutenberg` tool with the same `post_id`. There is currently no per-call `wp_url` override; the env var is the only host knob.
